kittenCare.title: Orphaned Kitten & Puppy Care
kittenCare.subtitle: How to keep newborn kittens and puppies alive through the first critical hours, until a rescue or veterinarian takes over.

sections.title: Confirm It Is Really Orphaned
sections.text: A mother often leaves for hours to hunt. Separating a healthy litter from its mother is the most common and most harmful mistake — wait and watch first.
bullets: Observe from a distance for two to four hours before intervening.
Warm, quiet babies with round bellies are being fed; cold crying ones are not.
Call a rescue before removing a litter — they often have a nursing mother available.

sections.title: Warm It Before You Feed It
sections.text: A cold baby cannot digest milk, and feeding it in that state can be fatal. Warmth always comes first.
bullets: Use a hot water bottle or heat pad, well wrapped, at one end of a box.
Leave half the box unheated so the baby can move away if it gets too warm.
Aim for 30 to 32 °C in the first week, and keep water away from the heat source.

sections.title: Feed on a Schedule, Upright
sections.text: Use only kitten or puppy milk replacer from a pet shop or pharmacy — cow’s milk causes diarrhoea and dehydration. Feed the baby lying on its stomach, never on its back like a human infant, and let it suck rather than squeezing the bottle.

sections.title: Help It Toilet
sections.text: Newborns cannot urinate or defecate by themselves; their mother would normally lick them. You replace that stimulation after every single feed.
bullets: Rub the genital area gently with a warm damp cotton pad for about a minute.
Expect urine after every feed and at least one stool a day.
No output, a hard belly, or crying while toileting needs veterinary help today.

sections.title: Keep Everything Clean
sections.text: Very young babies have almost no immune defence, so hygiene protects them more than any medicine you can buy.
bullets: Wash your hands before handling and keep the bedding dry.
Prepare only what one feed needs and never store leftover formula.
Wash bottles and teats in hot soapy water and rinse thoroughly after use.

sections.title: Escalate Early
sections.text: Fading happens fast — a quiet, cold baby may have only a couple of hours. Contact a rescue or clinic the same day rather than waiting for it to deteriorate.

checklist.title: Feeding reference
items: Week 1: every 2 to 3 hours around the clock, roughly 2 to 4 ml per feed.
Week 2: every 3 to 4 hours, roughly 5 to 7 ml per feed.
Weeks 3 to 4: every 4 to 5 hours, following the replacer packaging by weight.
From week 4: start weaning onto a gruel of replacer and wet food — ask a rescue for a plan.

kittenCare.disclaimer: Amounts are a starting point for healthy newborns. Weigh the baby daily and follow your veterinarian’s advice if it stops gaining weight.
